name: Kettlebell Swing
summary: A ballistic hip-hinge exercise using explosive extension of the posterior chain to project a kettlebell forward to chest height.

setup: Place the kettlebell on the floor about one foot in front of you.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and hinge back at the hips with a neutral spine.
Grip the kettlebell handle with both hands using an overhand grip, tilting the bell back toward you while engaging your lats.
steps: Hike the kettlebell dynamically back between your legs high in the groin, keeping your forearms in contact with your inner thighs.
Explosively extend your hips and knees to drive the kettlebell forward and up.
Stand tall at the top of the swing with glutes and core fully braced, letting the bell float momentarily to roughly chest height without lifting it with your arms.
Allow the kettlebell to freefall back down, waiting until your forearms touch your hips before hinging back to absorb the load into your posterior chain for the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Inhale sharply through your nose during the backswing, and forcefully exhale through pursed lips at the top of hip extension.
cues: Hike the bell high into the zipper.
Snap the hips and stand like a plank.
Tame the arc; don't lift with the arms.

common_faults.fault: Squatting the swing by dropping the hips too low and excessively bending the knees.
common_faults.correction: Keep the shins nearly vertical and push the hips backward in a pure hinge pattern.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the kettlebell with the shoulders and arms rather than projecting it from the hips.
common_faults.correction: Treat your arms purely as ropes or loose straps; all vertical momentum must come from the hip drive.

common_faults.fault: Hinging too early on the descent, exposing the lower back to excessive shear stress.
common_faults.correction: Play chicken with the bell: stand tall until the kettlebell nearly hits your hips before hinging backward.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lumbar spine at the apex of the swing.
common_faults.correction: Finish in a rigid standing plank with ribs pulled down, glutes squeezed, and abs braced.

precautions: Ensure chalk or a secure grip is used to prevent the kettlebell from slipping out of the hands.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the backswing and avoid rounding the lower back under load.
